content: The dosage of pyrimethamine (DARAPRIM) for the treatment of toxoplasmosis must be carefully tailored to achieve maximum therapeutic efficacy while minimizing adverse effects. At the required dosage levels, there is significant variability in individual tolerance to the drug. Younger patients generally tolerate higher doses better than older individuals. It is strongly recommended to administer folinic acid concurrently in all patients to mitigate potential side effects. The initial dosage is typically maintained for 1 to 3 weeks, depending on the patient’s response and tolerance to the therapy. After this period, the dosage may be reduced to approximately half of the initial dose for each drug and continued for an additional 4 to 5 weeks. For pediatric patients, the recommended dosage of DARAPRIM is 1 mg/kg/day, divided into two equal daily doses. After 2 to 4 days, this dose may be reduced by half and continued for approximately one month. The usual pediatric dosage of sulfonamides is administered in conjunction with DARAPRIM. For the treatment of acute malaria, DARAPRIM is not recommended as a standalone therapy. Fast-acting schizonticides, such as chloroquine or quinine, are indicated for the treatment of acute malaria. However, DARAPRIM, at a dosage of 25 mg daily for 2 days in combination with a sulfonamide, can help initiate transmission control and suppress non-falciparum malaria. DARAPRIM is only recommended for patients infected in regions where susceptible Plasmodium species are present. In situations where DARAPRIM must be used alone in semi-immune individuals, the adult dosage for acute malaria is 50 mg daily for 2 days. For children aged 4 to 10 years, the recommended dosage is 25 mg daily for 2 days. Regardless of the treatment approach, clinical cure should be followed by a once-weekly chemoprophylaxis regimen, as described below, for at least 10 weeks in all cases. The chemoprophylaxis dosage is 25 mg (1/4 tablet) once weekly.
